title.abbrev: YANG for NETCONF Clients and Servers

front.title: A YANG Data Model for NETCONF Clients and Servers

abstract.t: This document presents two YANG modules: one module to configure a Network Configuration Protocol (NETCONF) client and the other module to configure a NETCONF server. These modules support both the Secure Shell (SSH) and TLS transport protocols; they also support both standard NETCONF and NETCONF Call Home connections.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: This document presents two YANG modules : one module to configure a NETCONF client and the other module to configure a NETCONF server. These modules support both NETCONF-over-SSH and NETCONF-over-TLS as well as NETCONF Call Home connections .

section.name: Relation to Other RFCs
section.t: This document presents two YANG modules that are part of a collection of RFCs that work together to, ultimately, support the configuration of both the clients and servers of both the NETCONF and RESTCONF protocols.

Primary dependency relationships between the YANG groupings defined in the various RFCs are presented in the below diagram. In some cases, a document may define secondary groupings that introduce dependencies not illustrated in the diagram. The labels in the diagram are a shorthand name for the defining RFC. The citation reference for the shorthand name is provided in .

Please note that the arrows in the diagram point from referencer to referenced. For example, the "crypto-types" RFC does not have any dependencies, whilst the "keystore" RFC depends on the "crypto-types" RFC.

section.name: Specification Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

section.name: Adherence to the NMDA
section.t: This document is compliant with the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA) . For instance, as described in and , trust anchors and keys installed during manufacturing are expected to appear in <operational> () and <system> if implemented.

section.name: The "ietf-netconf-client" YANG Module
section.t: The NETCONF client YANG data model presented in this section supports both clients initiating connections to servers and clients listening for connections from servers calling home, using either the SSH or TLS transport protocol.
YANG feature statements are used to enable implementations to advertise which potentially uncommon parts of the data model the NETCONF client supports.

section.name: Data Model Overview
section.t: This section provides an overview of the "ietf-netconf-client" YANG module in terms of its features and groupings.

section.name: Features
section.t: The following diagram lists all the "feature" statements defined in the "ietf-netconf-client" module:
section.sourcecode: Features: +-- ssh-initiate +-- tls-initiate +-- ssh-listen +-- tls-listen +-- central-netconf-client-supported
section.t: The diagram above uses syntax that is similar to but not defined in .

section.name: Groupings
section.t: The "ietf-netconf-client" module defines the following "grouping" statements:
Each of these groupings are presented in the following subsections.

section.name: The "netconf-client-initiate-stack-grouping" Grouping
section.t: The following tree diagram illustrates the "netconf-client-initiate-stack-grouping" grouping:
section.sourcecode: grouping netconf-client-initiate-stack-grouping: +-- (transport) +--:(ssh) {ssh-initiate}? | +-- ssh | +-- tcp-client-parameters | | +---u tcpc:tcp-client-grouping | +-- ssh-client-parameters | | +---u sshc:ssh-client-grouping | +-- netconf-client-parameters | +--u ncc:netconf-client-grouping +--:(tls) {tls-initiate}? +-- tls +-- tcp-client-parameters | +---u tcpc:tcp-client-grouping +-- tls-client-parameters | +---u tlsc:tls-client-grouping +-- netconf-client-parameters +---u ncc:netconf-client-grouping
section.t: Comments:

ul.li: The "netconf-client-initiate-stack-grouping" defines the configuration for a full NETCONF protocol stack for NETCONF clients that initiate connections to NETCONF servers (as opposed to receiving call-home connections).
The "transport" choice node enables either the SSH or TLS transport to be configured, with each option enabled by a "feature" statement.

section.name: The "netconf-client-listen-stack-grouping" Grouping
section.t: The following tree diagram illustrates the "netconf-client-listen-stack-grouping" grouping:
section.sourcecode: grouping netconf-client-listen-stack-grouping: +-- (transport) +--:(ssh) {ssh-listen}? | +-- ssh | +-- tcp-server-parameters | | +---u tcps:tcp-server-grouping | +-- ssh-client-parameters | | +---u sshc:ssh-client-grouping | +-- netconf-client-parameters | +--u ncc:netconf-client-grouping +--:(tls) {tls-listen}? +-- tls +-- tcp-server-parameters | +---u tcps:tcp-server-grouping +-- tls-client-parameters | +---u tlsc:tls-client-grouping +-- netconf-client-parameters +---u ncc:netconf-client-grouping
section.t: Comments:

ul.li: The "netconf-client-listen-stack-grouping" defines the configuration for a full NETCONF protocol stack for NETCONF clients that receive call-home connections from NETCONF servers.
The "transport" choice node enables either the SSH or TLS transport to be configured, with each option enabled by a "feature" statement.

section.name: The "netconf-client-app-grouping" Grouping
section.t: The following tree diagram illustrates the "netconf-client-app-grouping" grouping:
section.sourcecode: grouping netconf-client-app-grouping: +-- initiate! {ssh-initiate or tls-initiate}? | +-- netconf-server* [name] | +-- name string | +-- endpoints | | +-- endpoint* [name] | | +-- name string | | +---u netconf-client-initiate-stack-grouping | +-- connection-type | | +-- (connection-type) | | +--:(persistent-connection) | | | +-- persistent! | | +--:(periodic-connection) | | +-- periodic! | | +-- period? uint16 | | +-- anchor-time? yang:date-and-time | | +-- idle-timeout? uint16 | +-- reconnect-strategy | +-- start-with? enumeration | +-- max-wait? uint16 | +-- max-attempts? uint8 +-- listen! {ssh-listen or tls-listen}? +-- idle-timeout? uint16 +-- endpoints +-- endpoint* [name] +-- name string +---u netconf-client-listen-stack-grouping
section.t: Comments:

ul.li: The "netconf-client-app-grouping" defines the configuration for a NETCONF client that supports both initiating connections to NETCONF servers and receiving call-home connections from NETCONF servers.
Both the "initiate" and "listen" subtrees are predicated by "feature" statements.

section.name: Protocol-Accessible Nodes
section.t: The following tree diagram lists all the protocol-accessible nodes defined in the "ietf-netconf-client" module:
Comments:

ul.li: Protocol-accessible nodes are those nodes that are accessible when the module is "implemented", as described in .
The top-level node "netconf-client" is additionally constrained by the feature "central-netconf-client-supported".

The reason "netconf-client-app-grouping" exists separately from the protocol-accessible nodes definition is to enable instances of "netconf-client-app-grouping" to be instantiated in other locations, as may be needed or desired by some modules.

section.name: Considerations for the "ietf-netconf-client" YANG Module
section.t: This section is modeled after the template described in .

The "ietf-netconf-client" YANG module defines a data model that is designed to be accessed via YANG-based management protocols, such as the Network Configuration Protocol (NETCONF) and RESTCONF . These YANG-based management protocols (1) have to use a secure transport layer (e.g., Secure Shell (SSH) , TLS , and QUIC ) and (2) have to use mutual authentication.

The Network Configuration Access Control Model (NACM) provides the means to restrict access for particular NETCONF or RESTCONF users to a preconfigured subset of all available NETCONF or RESTCONF protocol operations and content.

None of the writable data nodes defined in this YANG module are considered sensitive or vulnerable in network environments. The NACM "default-deny-write" extension has not been set for any data nodes defined in this module.

None of the readable data nodes defined in this YANG module are considered sensitive or vulnerable in network environments. The NACM "default-deny-all" extension has not been set for any data nodes defined in this module.
This YANG module does not define any RPCs, actions, or notifications; thus, the security consideration for such is not provided here.

This YANG module uses groupings from other YANG modules that define nodes that may be considered sensitive or vulnerable in network environments. Refer to the Security Considerations of , , and for information as to which nodes may be considered sensitive or vulnerable in network environments.
This YANG module uses groupings defined in other RFCs that define data nodes that do set the NACM "default-deny-all" and "default-deny-write" extensions.

section.name: Considerations for the "ietf-netconf-server" YANG Module
section.t: This section is modeled after the template described in .

The "ietf-netconf-server" YANG module defines a data model that is designed to be accessed via YANG-based management protocols, such as the Network Configuration Protocol (NETCONF) and RESTCONF . These YANG-based management protocols (1) have to use a secure transport layer (e.g., Secure Shell (SSH) , TLS , and QUIC ) and (2) have to use mutual authentication.

The Network Configuration Access Control Model (NACM) provides the means to restrict access for particular NETCONF or RESTCONF users to a preconfigured subset of all available NETCONF or RESTCONF protocol operations and content.

None of the writable data nodes defined in this YANG module are considered sensitive or vulnerable in network environments. The NACM "default-deny-write" extension has not been set for any data nodes defined in this module.

None of the readable data nodes defined in this YANG module are considered sensitive or vulnerable in network environments. The NACM "default-deny-all" extension has not been set for any data nodes defined in this module.
This YANG module does not define any RPCs, actions, or notifications; thus, the security consideration for such is not provided here.

This YANG module uses groupings from other YANG modules that define nodes that may be considered sensitive or vulnerable in network environments. Refer to the Security Considerations of , , , and for information as to which nodes may be considered sensitive or vulnerable in network environments.
This YANG module uses groupings defined in other RFCs that define data nodes that do set the NACM "default-deny-all" and "default-deny-write" extensions.
